ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a cyclic structure containing two oxygen atoms; the two adjacent carbons on the left respectively bear R and R1 substituents, and each also bears one hydrogen. The right side is connected to a fragment containing P(OMe)3; there is a positive charge label and multiple curved arrows in the figure, indicating electron movement from the two C–O bonds and the adjacent bond system. Reasoning: After pushing according to the arrows, the two C–O bonds on the left break, and a C=C double bond forms between the two adjacent carbons on the left; R and R1, as generic substituents, are represented by wildcard [*] in SMILES. The shown ring cleavage gives a trans/crossed alkene configuration, so it is written as [*]/C([H])=C([H])\[*]. The phosphorus-containing fragment on the right rearranges into a charged phosphate ester/carbonyl-like fragment, in which oxygen is negatively charged, phosphorus is positively charged, and the three methoxy groups remain connected to phosphorus, written as [O-]C([P+](OC)(OC)OC)=O. The two products are disconnected from each other and are connected with a dot.

method.method_draft: Describe the image structure, then trace each curved arrow to update bonds: remove the C–O bonds indicated by the arrows, create the double bond between the two left carbon atoms, and convert the phosphorus-containing side into the indicated charged phosphate/carbonyl-like fragment.
